findings.detail: The completion timestamp becomes last_success even when a scan itself exceeds maximum_scan_age_seconds. A130s initial scan is accepted with a120s lease; a long periodic scan can likewise erase a missed stale interval.
findings.requested_fix: Record successful scan start and completion separately, bound scan duration, and latch timeout failures before refreshing the successful-scan lease. Initial/final scans must enforce the same finite contract.
findings.title: Completed slow scan renews lease without bounding scan duration

findings.detail: The writer checks state only before waiting on an unbounded callback lock. A blocked periodic scan allows its lease to expire; after the scan returns, last_success is reset and the waiting write is accepted.
findings.requested_fix: Use bounded lock acquisition with repeated cheap wall/failure/freshness checks, and revalidate after acquiring the lock before running or accepting the prospective-write scan. Do not silently renew a lease already missed while waiting.
findings.title: Prospective write waits indefinitely for callback lock and can cross freshness deadline

source_clarifications: Periodic scan cadence is30seconds after completion, so a27.3second scan yields about57.3seconds between starts; the receipt discloses this difference.

Numeric caps and source algorithm remain unchanged, but this is still cooperative sampled protection; a stuck callback cannot be safely canceled as a Python thread, so ROOT outer guardian stays authoritative.
Integration must give this wrapper exclusive ownership of the original callback; remaining aliases must not invoke its mutable next_check and status writer concurrently.
Caller must close the wrapper before reporting completion and must propagate close failure; no live installation has been reviewed.
